I met your dad, Ian, when we both joined a beginners' tennis club.
So we both started to play tennis as adults in our 20s.

And then we came back, we got together, and the rest is history, as they say.
Yeah. Oh, wow.
Yeah, obviously I know this story, but it's still interesting.
Yeah. I heard that there was a little bit of competition, actually.
Really? Yeah. Who with?
Oh, it's a secret between me and Dad, that.
Oh, right. Okay, so where did you go on your first date?
We went to a little pub in Leicestershire called The Reservoir,
which is on the edge of a reservoir in Leicester.
And we had a nice drink there.
And then we went on and we had

which is fantastic for curries.
And it was memorable because Ian had a vindaloo.
Yeah. He had a vindaloo, which is a very,
very hot curry, and about three jugs of water.
So it was quite funny.
So, was he trying to show off?
Yes. I think he was trying to impress me with,
you know, how spicy a curry he could eat.
Right. "Look how spicy my curries are."
Yeah, that's quite funny.
But he did drink a lot of water, which is not the best thing.

Because you made up your own language, right,
and only I could understand what you were saying.

I don't know what mine is, so don't worry if you don't know.

My best friend at school was Anne Harper,

It was an exam that we used to have.
We still have it technically in some places.

That's sad.

like, growing up as a child, I'm in my own world.

I was at an inner-city school that, you know, wasn't remarkable.

and then suddenly in a very posh school. Yeah.

relatively poor kid, right, in a posh school?

because at my junior school everybody was the same, really.
But I think the impact it has had is that I like to
